name: deepseek-harness-sessions
description: Unofficial: run DeepSeek Harness (dsh) as a native agent session in VS Code, alongside Claude Code and Codex.

chatSessions.name: deepseek-harness
chatSessions.description: Sessions run by your own dsh install

deepseekHarness.executable.markdownDescription: Absolute path to your `dsh` executable. Empty resolves it from `PATH`, then from `#deepseekHarness.checkoutPath#`. This extension never ships a dsh of its own.

deepseekHarness.checkoutPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a built deepseek-harness checkout, used when `dsh` is not on `PATH`. Its `apps/cli/lib/bin.js` is run with `node`.

deepseekHarness.home.markdownDescription: Overrides `$DSH_HOME`. Empty uses your real dsh home, so the editor sees the profiles, settings, credentials and history you already have.

deepseekHarness.historyPageMessages.markdownDescription: How many past messages to load when opening a session. Kept small on purpose: `session.history` also returns every token-level chunk event behind those messages, which is ~100% of the payload and is discarded on arrival. Raising this makes opening a long session slower, not richer.

deepseekHarness.extraArgs.markdownDescription: Extra arguments appended to `dsh web`. The bind host and port are not configurable: the server has no auth, so it is always loopback on an ephemeral port.
